title: opt-125m: prefill and eight decode steps

context.workload: facebook/opt-125m in fp16, batch size 1: a 104-token prompt (prefill), then 8 greedy decode steps reusing the KV cache
context.settings: Recorded after one identical warm-up run, with torch.profiler collecting CPU ops, GPU kernels and GPU memory. Profiling adds overhead to every CPU-side op, so CPU times here are longer than in an unprofiled run.
context.source: Recorded with tools/profile_example.py and reduced with tools/trace_extract.py; the CPU lane shows only top-level PyTorch ops, not the ops nested inside them.

annotations.title: Start here: one prefill, eight decode steps
annotations.text: The prompt goes through the model once (prefill), then each decode step produces one more token. Prefill and every decode step launch the same 207 GPU kernels; prefill takes about 9.5 ms and each decode step about 6.9 ms.

annotations.title: The GPU is mostly waiting
annotations.text: The kernels inside this 6.9 ms step add up to about 0.67 ms, so the GPU is busy for roughly a tenth of the step. The other lanes show where the time goes instead: the CPU is busy for most of the step.

annotations.title: Hundreds of small ops on the CPU
annotations.text: Each decode step dispatches 342 top-level PyTorch ops (73 of them are linear layers), which occupy about 4.9 ms of the step. The short gaps between ops are Python running the model code. With a model this small, the per-op cost on the CPU is larger than the work each op sends to the GPU.

annotations.title: The longest kernel in each decode step
annotations.text: About 24 µs, once per decode step, right at the end. Its position and size are consistent with the output projection from the 768-dimensional hidden state to the 50,272-token vocabulary, the largest matrix in the model. I have not confirmed this against the op that launched it.

annotations.title: The KV cache grows by copying
annotations.text: There are 24 of these concatenation kernels in every step: one for the keys and one for the values in each of the 12 layers. The cache grows by concatenating the new token onto the old tensor, which copies what is already there. At this sequence length each copy takes about 2 µs.

annotations.title: Memory: one token of KV cache per step
annotations.text: In the memory lane, allocated memory at the end of each decode step is about 0.035 MiB higher than the step before. That matches one token of KV cache: 12 layers × (key + value) × 768 values × 2 bytes = 36,864 bytes. The drop of about 10 MiB early in decode 1 is consistent with the prefill's logits for all 104 prompt positions being freed (104 × 50,272 × 2 bytes ≈ 10 MiB).
